sqlInjection.title: SQL Injection in Login Form
sqlInjection.description: The login form is vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. User input is not properly sanitized before being used in SQL queries.
sqlInjection.impact: An attacker could bypass authentication, extract sensitive data, or execute arbitrary SQL commands on the database.
sqlInjection.recommendation: Use prepared statements or parameterized queries instead of directly incorporating user input into SQL queries. Implement input validation and sanitization.

sqlInjection.title: SQL Injection in Search Function
sqlInjection.description: The search function is vulnerable to SQL injection. User input from the search field is inserted directly into SQL queries.
sqlInjection.impact: Attackers could extract sensitive data, modify database contents, or potentially gain access to the underlying server.
sqlInjection.recommendation: Use prepared statements with parameterized queries. Apply proper input validation and consider using an ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) library.

sqlInjection.title: Blind SQL Injection Vulnerability
sqlInjection.description: The profile page is vulnerable to blind SQL injection attacks through the user ID parameter.
sqlInjection.impact: Even without direct error messages, attackers can extract data by observing differences in application responses.
sqlInjection.recommendation: Use parameterized queries and implement proper input validation. Consider using a Web Application Firewall (WAF) as an additional security layer.

xss.title: Stored XSS in Comment System
xss.description: The comment system stores user input without proper sanitization, allowing attackers to inject malicious JavaScript.
xss.impact: Attackers can steal session cookies, redirect users to malicious sites, or perform actions on behalf of other users.
xss.recommendation: Sanitize user input before storing in the database. Use HTML encoding when displaying user-generated content. Consider using a Content Security Policy.

xss.title: Reflected XSS in Error Messages
xss.description: Error messages reflect user input without proper encoding, allowing for XSS attacks via specifically crafted URLs.
xss.impact: Attackers can create malicious links that execute JavaScript in victims' browsers when clicked.
xss.recommendation: Encode all output that contains user input. Use a templating system that automatically escapes output.

xss.title: DOM-based XSS Vulnerability
xss.description: Client-side JavaScript code insecurely processes URL fragment identifiers, leading to DOM-based XSS.
xss.impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary JavaScript by crafting specific URLs with malicious fragments.
xss.recommendation: Use safe DOM manipulation methods and sanitize all data before inserting it into the DOM.
